Hi Sarah,

Great to speak earlier — thanks for taking the time. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align with FintechCo's security & privacy needs: 

Summary of ask from call:
- FintechCo needs strong masking/redaction for PII in request/response logs (names, SSNs, payment instrument data)
- Avoid storing unredacted headers/trace IDs that could link to user identifiers
- Short retention window for logs used for debugging (preferably < 30 days) with longer retention for aggregated metrics
- Want a documented design and a short runbook for incident response

What Redwood can offer (high-level):
- Configurable redaction pipeline (regex + schema-aware redaction) that runs before logs hit persistent stores
- Option to strip headers and trace IDs or hash them with a salted HMAC for correlation without exposing raw identifiers
- Retention controls per log class (request traces vs. aggregated metrics) and per-environment (prod vs. staging)
- Export controls to prevent logs from leaving the configured region; can support US-only residency for logs

3) We can produce a proof-of-concept configuration that demonstrates redaction on a sample request/response set.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal sync, see answers below and attached design doc for the redaction flow. Quick summary first, then details: 

Summary answers:
- Salt management: We support both Redwood-managed salts and customer-managed salts stored in customer KMS. For customers that require key ownership we offer a KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) so salts never leave the customer-controlled key.
- Trace IDs: We recommend hashing trace IDs with a per-customer salt + HMAC (configurable per-tenant). This gives you correlation within your tenant without exposing a reversible identifier externally.
- Headers & routing: We can perform selective header stripping at the ingestion proxy and maintain a transient, in-memory routing context that is not persisted. Headers that are required for downstream routing can be hashed instead of stored in plaintext.
- Retention controls: Retention windows are configurable per-log-class via the Redwood Console for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we can enforce via configuration (we'll include a sample retention policy). You can set raw request/response retention to 30 days and aggregated metrics to 365 days.
- Region controls: We support region-restricted log stores; logs can be configured to stay in US regions only.

Next steps / deliverables we've attached:
- redaction-design.pdf — detailed diagram + sample config snippets (attached)
- SOC2-security-answers.docx — answers to your checklist items (attached)
- We can run a 30-minute walkthrough on Thu 2026-03-05 at 9:30 AM PT with Rishi and Dev — does that work for you?

Implementation notes (short):
- Redaction pipeline: ingress proxy -> schema-aware extractor -> redaction engine (regex + PII model) -> salted-hash correlator -> persistent store. Redaction happens before the write to persistent storage.
- Latency: inline redaction adds negligible overhead for typical payloads (< 5ms p99) because we use compiled regex paths and an optimized PII classifier. For very large payloads we recommend sampling or async redaction options.
- Proof-of-concept: we can provide a sample config and a small dataset to demo on your side; this will include a sandboxed log store in US-only region.

Attachments: redaction-design.pdf (diagram + config examples), SOC2-security-answers.docx
